Its one prospective prediction (efavirenz, AUC 68% of baseline) became the label's no-dose-adjustment statement for moderate CYP3A inducers without a clinical study, a regulator reliance on the in-silico model that stays untested in humans, so no fresh entry. dose.model: Rat, dog and monkey toxicology and safety-pharmacology package

First-in-human study AV-951-03-B01 is not on ClinicalTrials.gov, so registry_date is null. model_first_use_year for the tox package is set to 2011, the first public reference to it (this abstract); the monkey study itself began in 2003 (FDA review) but was not public.
dose.note: The first-in-human trial reported animal data had mispredicted toxicity: the 2.0 mg start dose gave grade 3 hypertension and proteinuria DLTs; hypertension DLT recurred at the 1.5 mg MTD. Not a retrodiction: for dose only tivozanib's own earlier patient result would count, and none preceded this first-in-human trial.

dose.judgement: Dose, not safety: the monkey package did predict a blood-pressure rise but placed it far above the human dose, so under 'count the harm once' the misplaced margin is scored here. Decision 16: the stated cardiovascular NOAEL (HED 5.8 mg/day) exceeded the effective dose, yet grade 3 hypertension DLT occurred at the 1.5 mg MTD that became the recommended dose, so toxicity at the effective exposure is contra, blocked_by toxicity. Efficacy is not affected (the dose was given). The existing safety same (FDA 2021, re-dated 2017 by the checker) scores the same harm by direction; the checker should decide whether it stays. Patient side is a mixed solid-tumour phase I (CRC enrolled); imported_from is not allowed on dose, so the population field carries it.
dose.reason: Animal data mispredicted toxicity at start dose

Monkey detail from FDA 212904 review: 'A dose of 3 mg/kg resulted in increases in systolic, diastolic and mean arterial blood pressure 90 minutes post-dose.'
safety.judgement: Same in direction with a misplaced margin (monkey effect at 39x the human dose). Under the 2026-11-09 imported-harm ruling, this disease's patients were measured, so BATON-CRC's registry AE table (posted 2015-04-03) replaces the RCC NDA data and imported_from is cleared. Year is 2017, when the model side first became public (EMA Fotivda EPAR, 22 Jun 2017, per the checker); the FDA 2021 review is the later model source. The checker adjudicated 'drop' under count-the-harm-once (dose index 5 already scores this misplaced margin); entries cannot be deleted under this pass, so the overlap stays flagged.

safety.note: Imported-harm ruling: CRC patients were measured (BATON-CRC, 43.5% hypertension with tivozanib vs 28.7% with bevacizumab), so they replace the RCC data. Monkey BP rise predicted it; status unchanged, re-dated 2017.

safety.magnitude_basis: missed harm; no model number to scale (patient side: 'The most common Grade 3-4 AE was hypertension, which occurred more frequently on the fruquintinib arm relative to placebo (14% vs. 1%)')
safety.confidence_note: The dog cardiovascular study was single-dose (up to 0.34 mg/kg, about 2x the clinical dose on BSA), a design that cannot show a harm that takes days to develop; the 13-week dog study reported no blood-pressure data. Scored as silence contradicted because monkeys (tivozanib) and dogs can show VEGFR-TKI hypertension. The package did predict haemorrhage (rat adrenal haemorrhage, dog red faeces/discharge), physeal thickening and embryo-fetal toxicity, which hold in the label.
safety.judgement: One drug's contra beats another's same on the same track, so the tox track ends contra despite the tivozanib monkey match; the two drugs' non-rodent species differ (monkey vs dog), which is the main reason this could instead be split into two tracks. Proteinuria and hand-foot syndrome were also unpredicted but are not separately scored.
safety.model: Rat, dog and monkey toxicology and safety-pharmacology package
